thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High error rates observed for enterprise tenant 'sirocco' in eu-west-1 (dedicated pool dp-sirocco-eu1). Severity: P1. Auto-escalation to oncall.

sre_june: I'm on it, seeing 502 spikes from the pool. Dashboard: increased 95th latency + connection resets. Starting initial triage.

oncall-ryan: joining. Are customer-facing endpoints returning 5xx or timeouts? Customer reported 30% of requests failing.

eng_tariq: Confirmed from logs: requests to model backend are timing out at the inference runtime. CPU on the pool nodes is normal, GPU load high and queued. Looks like a warm capacity pressure + KV cache thrash.

alex_pm: Customer (Sirocco Corp) on Dedicated Enterprise (VPC) — they have SLAs. They reported partial outage for EU customers. We need mitigation plan and customer comms.

support_lei: Customer ops says they're seeing increased client retries and some degraded responses. They're asking for ETA and if there will be a DNS cutover.

sre_june: Quick mitigation options: 1) Shift traffic to their warm pool in us-east-1 (dp-sirocco-us1) via traffic manager; 2) DNS cutover to fallback ingress with pre-warmed nodes; 3) Scale up dedicated pool (slow). We should prefer traffic shift + DNS TTL tricks to keep latency reasonable.

infra-bot: warm-pool-status: dp-sirocco-us1 healthy (10/10 warm nodes ready). dp-sirocco-eu1 current capacity: 75% saturated, queue depth high.

oncall-ryan: Let's do a controlled traffic shift. Steps: lower DNS TTL for the tenant, update CNAME to traffic-manager, shift 30% -> 70% gradually, monitor errors. If latency acceptable, continue until 100%.

eng_tariq: Preparing traffic-manager job. I need confirmation to lower TTL — current TTL is 300s. Lowering to 60s now.

eng_tariq: (action) run:
```
# change in Route53 console / API
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"sirocco.api.redwood.example","Type":"CNAME","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"tm.sirocco-internal.redwood.example"}]}}]}'
```

infra-bot: DNS change submitted (change-id CZZ-98765). Propagation expected within ~60s after change becomes INSYNC.

support_lei: Pushed a note to Sirocco ops: "We're initiating traffic shift to a warm failover region to mitigate errors. You'll see client IPs served from a different region for a short time. We'll update with progress." Customer replied: "Please proceed, we need stability now."

eng_tariq: Kicking off traffic-manager plan: initial weight: eu-west-1=70, us-east-1=30. Instrumentation: synthetic requests hitting edge -> model -> verify 200 OK + token consistency.

sre_june: Watch metrics: 5xx count, p95 latency, and model mismatch rates. Also watch egress costs — notify finance if long term.

oncall-ryan: I ran a smoke curl against the fallback endpoint after change:
```
curl -v https://sirocco.api.redwood.example/health
# result: HTTP/2 200 OK, backend: dp-sirocco-us1
```

eng_tariq: After 5 minutes: errors on eu-west dropped from 28% -> 6%. us-east 30% is serving with p95 ~210ms, acceptable.

alex_pm: Good. Begin gradual ramp to 100% over next 20 minutes if metrics hold. Prepare to execute a DNS CNAME cutover to permanently point at us-east ingress if pool scaling can't catch up.

infra-bot: Alert: a single node in dp-sirocco-eu1 restarted unexpectedly at 1825001402 — health checks recovered but queue backlog persisted.

sre_june: Noted. Add that to RCA later. For now, continuing ramp.

eng_tariq: Adjusted weights: eu-west-1=40, us-east-1=60.

oncall-ryan: After ramp: eu-west errors ~2%, us-east stable. I'll stand by for the DNS final cutover if needed.

support_lei: Customer ops: "Sirocco confirms traffic is flowing and errors are down. They want a post-mortem and confirmation of permanent fix timeline." Asked if we can schedule at EOD.

eng_tariq: We're opening a transient runbook item: make dp-sirocco-eu1 autoscale target + add one hot spare; investigate KV cache thrash causing GPU queuing. Will also test model quantization fallback to reduce GPU pressure.

alex_pm: Communicate to customer: short summary and ETA: expected permanent fix by tomorrow 10:00 UTC (engineering investigating root cause and will add capacity + config tweak). Drafting message.

eng_tariq: If we decide to do DNS cutover to point sirocco.api directly at failover ingress, we need to set CNAME TTL low (done) and update permanent record. Proposed change:
```
# permanent cutover
sirocco.api.redwood.example. CNAME -> ingress-us1.redwood.example. TTL=300
```
Will schedule after SRE signoff.

incident-bot: Reminder: update incident status in PagerDuty and assign incident owner.

sre_june: I've set incident owner: @sre_june. Updating PD with mitigations and initial timeline. PD incident link: https://pd.redwood.example/incidents/PD-8923

oncall-ryan: Handoff note for next shift: State = mitigated (traffic shifted to warm pool, errors <3%), Actions taken = DNS TTL lowered, traffic manager weights ramped, warm pool served ~100% temporarily. Next steps = scale eu pool + RCA. Please monitor for any regression and be ready to revert traffic manager if errors rise above 5%.

support_lei: Customer message sent: "We have shifted traffic to a warm failover region and are seeing recovery. Engineering is investigating root cause and will provide a timeline for a permanent fix. We'll follow up by EOD with an incident summary." Customer responded with :thumbsup:.

eng_tariq: Ticket opened: ENG-INC-1927. Investigations: runtime queue profiling, KV cache eviction patterns, node restart traces. I'll attach kernel and runtime logs.

infra-bot: Note: Scheduled warm capacity increase for dp-sirocco-eu1 requested (2 hot nodes). ETA for spin-up 12 minutes.

sre_june: Once the new nodes are up and warmed, we'll shift traffic back gradually. For now, keep routing as-is until we validate stability.

alex_pm: Adding a short customer-facing postmortem draft after RCA. Also planning follow-up meeting with Sirocco ops tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

oncall-ryan: Handing off to night oncall @sre_june (staying listed). Key alarms: error rate spike >5% or latency p95 >500ms. If it triggers, revert traffic-manager weights to eu-west=100 and open immediate page.

support_lei: Acknowledged. Will keep customer updated for night.

eng_tariq: Follow-up: As we brought up hot nodes, we observed cache warm-up reduces tail latency. We're seeing eu-west errors stabilize at ~0.8% and p95 back to baseline. Planning controlled reroute back over next 30m.

incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved -> mitigated. Please file postmortem in postmortems/ and link ENG-INC-1927. Resolution note: Traffic shifted to warm pool in us-east, additional hot nodes added to eu pool, root cause suspected runtime KV cache thrash causing GPU queueing. RCA pending.

sre_june: Closing the thread for now. Thanks everyone for fast response. I'll own the follow-ups and the postmortem.

customer_ops_brian: Thanks team — Sirocco appreciates the quick mitigation. We'll await the postmortem and will coordinate our own client-side retry/backoff guidance.
